rationale: I'm replacing the Fisher-z Pearson features with a tangent-space embedding of Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariances on CC200. This approach was the most reliable connectome pipeline in large rs-fMRI benchmarks (Dadi et al. 2019). It respects the geometry of covariance matrices and lowers between-subject variance. The shrinkage also keeps short scans (some sites have fewer timepoints than ROIs) and all-zero ROIs well-conditioned. The reference mean comes only from the training fold, and the classifier is unchanged.

ADHD-200 has large site differences, and they dominate the shared tangent-space reference. I'll whiten each subject's covariance by the Riemannian mean of its own site (Riemannian Procrustes/re-centering), so the classifier learns differences within each site. To keep the useful information that ADHD rates differ by site, I'll add a smoothed site log-odds prior from the training fold back onto the decision score.

Sex is a strong, well-documented ADHD covariate in ADHD-200, since most ADHD cases are boys, and age also matters. But one sex column appended to about 20k heavily regularized connectome features would get almost no weight. So I'll stack instead: grouped inner CV (using `ctx["groups_train"]`) produces out-of-fold scores from the tangent-space logistic regression, and a small second-stage logistic regression combines those scores with sex and age.
